subject: Sizing & mode decision follow-up: throughput, token mix, and VPC constraints
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex@nimblecommerce.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing & mode decision follow-up: throughput, token mix, and VPC constraints

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the few follow-ups we promised:

Summary from our side:
- Goal: production-grade recommendation for whether Nimble should go Hosted, Dedicated, or Private (VPC/on-prem) for search-and-assist.
- Primary constraints you highlighted: data residency (US-East), procurement timeline (~6–8 weeks), and a hard requirement for VPC peering if we go beyond hosted.
- Approx steady-state targets you shared: 90–120 TPS typical, up to 150 TPS short spikes; average prompt/completion token mix appeared to be ~60 prompt / 300–400 completion tokens.

Action items / clarifying questions (please reply inline):
1) Confirm steady-state TPS and % of traffic that’s short vs long completions (e.g., % with >800 completion tokens).
2) GPU preference: you mentioned H100s in passing — is that a hard requirement or a preference (H100 vs A100 vs quantized A100)?
3) VPC: are you planning VPC-only (no public internet egress to our hosted endpoint) or is hybrid acceptable (initially hosted with VPC peering later)?
4) Any compliance docs we should prioritize for procurement (SOC2, ISO27001, DPA)? Procurement email copied below — we’ll send a short evidence pack once we confirm mode.

Next steps we propose:
- If you confirm H100 preference and the TPS profile, we’ll scope a Dedicated sizing and send a preliminary pricing estimate (attached draft).
- If you prefer to evaluate costs first, we can run a short simulated workload on hosted to validate latency profiles before locking into Dedicated.

I attached the call notes export (nimble_poc_stats.csv) you shared — thanks for that.

Would you be able to respond to the four items above by EOD Wednesday? Happy to hop on a quick follow-up if helpful.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Turner <alex@nimblecommerce.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nimblecommerce.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing & mode decision follow-up: throughput, token mix, and VPC constraints

Soojin —

Thanks for the recap. Answers inline below: 

1) TPS: our conservative steady-state target is 90 TPS. We commonly see daily peaks (marketing campaigns) up to ~150 TPS for ~10–20 minutes. We estimate about 12% of requests produce very long completions (>800 tokens) — these are rare but important.

2) GPU: preference is H100 due to the attention patterns and long-context tests we ran; not a hard legal requirement, but performance matters. If there’s a meaningful cost delta and quantized A100s meet latency SLOs, we’re open to that as an alternative.

3) VPC: procurement requires VPC-only for production data flows. For a POC we can do hybrid (hosted endpoint) provided any customer data is pseudonymized. Production must be VPC peering with our AWS account in us-east-1.

4) Procurement: SOC2 type II and DPA docs will be required. Procurement contact (procurement@nimblecommerce.com) is copied.

Procurement timeline: 6–8 weeks after we accept SOW. Budget: TBD, but they asked us to get a model-level and capacity-level budget to review.

Attached: brief latency/SLAs doc we use internally (tiny PDF).

Happy to review your pricing and recommended configuration.

—Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Platform, Nimble Commerce
alex@nimblecommerce.com | +1 650-555-0112

Subject: Re: Sizing & mode decision follow-up: throughput, token mix, and VPC constraints

Alex —

Appreciate the detail, that’s really helpful. Two immediate responses and proposed next steps: 

Responses:
- H100 preference noted (we’ll baseline H100). We’ll also include an A100 quantized alternative for cost comparison.
- VPC-only production requirement understood — we’ll include a VPC deployment checklist and estimate network egress patterns for peering.
- SOC2 & DPA: we’ll package the evidence and send to procurement as a single zip (expect within 48 hours).

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood creates a brief Dedicated sizing doc with two configuration options: H100 baseline and quantized A100 cost-optimized. Expect a first-pass within 48 hours.
2) We’ll run a short latency simulation on hosted to cross-check your 90–150 TPS profile (optional; let me know if you want this).
3) Karthik (cc’d) will prepare a small Jupyter notebook to estimate GPU-hour and reserved pool size depending on token mix and concurrency; can you confirm we can upload sample logs to the drive link below?

If that all sounds good I’ll mark item as "deliverables due Fri 8/13" and send the SOW template to procurement for initial review.

Best,
Soojin
[Attachment: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v2.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex@nimblecommerce.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing & mode decision follow-up: throughput, token mix, and VPC constraints

Alex / Soojin —

Quick technical note from engineering side. Based on the numbers shared (steady 90 TPS, spikes to 150 TPS, ~12% >800-token completions) here’s a starting sizing sketch: 

- Baseline option (H100): target p95 latency <200ms for 90 TPS steady assuming batching + KV cache for prefix reuse. Estimate: 4 H100 GPUs in a reserved pool with headroom for autoscale to 6 for spike windows.
- Cost-optimized option (Quantized A100): 6 quantized A100s, slightly higher p95 (200–250ms) but ~30% lower unit cost.

Questions that materially change sizing:
- QPS distribution across 24h (is 90 TPS uniform or concentrated?). If concentrated in short bursts we should plan for higher autoscale headroom.
- % of calls that are streaming vs non-streaming (streaming paths affect throughput more).
- Any hard p95 SLO (Alex, you mentioned a target earlier).

Upload location: please place sample request logs (anonymized) into the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-nimble-poc — I’ll run the notebook on them and return a short table of recommended reserved pool sizes.

I’ll produce the notebook and initial table by EOD Thursday and include the roofline of cost per 1M tokens for both configs.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124
